build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

comments.text: The utilities program's first instruction, JMP utils_main. The program is T8/L20, 14 pages, loaded to $7E00-$8BFF from the title's Utils (start-up $81EF-$81F7) by load_program ($2890), which jumps to the load address in the header's bytes +3/+4. The auto symbol came from the fast loader's LDA $7E00,X operand ($FF6C), which still points here.
Header bytes load_program reads from the program's first sector: +3/+4 the load address $7E00, +5 the page count $0E (14), so the program fills $7E00-$8BFF. Not executed: the JMP at $7E00 skips them.

Main loop of the utilities: utils_menu_show (menu 0, 'Copy Restart Start'), utils_screen, word-wrapped output ($0302), then forever read_key ($022A, the key in $18) and menu_key ($02DE), which runs the selected item's handler from the tables at utils_menu_handlers. Copy and Restart come back here, and so does Start after a back-arrow at its prompts; once Start has a side it ends in load_program and does not come back.

Draws the utilities screen: $9F = $FF, then engine entry $04E1 ($0AA1) draws the 18-segment bar at columns 38-39, rows 17 to 0 ($9F is the Geiger reading; $FF/8 is past the 18 segments, so every segment is drawn plain, $7E/$5B); a frame from column 0, row 0 to column 37, row 17 (draw_frame $0398); the text window inside it, columns 1-36 and pixel lines 8-135 ($25-$28), cleared by clear_window ($025C).

Shows menu 0, 'Copy Restart Start': $3E/$3F = utils_menu_texts, $40/$41 = utils_menu_handlers, menu $3B = 0, selection $39 = 0, last visible item $3A = 2, then draw_menu_bar ($02E7). Also the handler of the copy menu's Exit and of its hidden back-arrow key (copy_menu_handlers), so either returns to menu 0.

Menu text table for $3E/$3F (utils_menu_show), one word per menu number $3B: 0 menu0_text 'Copy Restart Start', 1 copy_menu_text, 2 menu2_text 'Reading.', 3 menu3_text 'Writing.', 4 menu4_text 'Formatting.'; menus 2-4 are status lines the copier shows while it works.

Handler-table table for $40/$41: one word per menu, 0 main_menu_handlers, 1 copy_menu_handlers, 2 and 3 status_menu_handlers. Menu 4 has no word: run_menu_item would read the first bytes of menu0_text ($6F43), but no key reaches menu_key while 'Formatting.' is shown.
Menu 0's bar: 'Copy Restart Start', $00, then $00 for no hidden hot keys. C, R, S (or RETURN on the selected item) run copy_command, restart_command, start_command; ',' and '.' move the selection.
Menu 2, a status line: 16 spaces and 'Reading.', $00, $00 (no hot keys); status_bar_reading shows it while copy_disk_op reads a master sector.
Menu 3, a status line: 16 spaces and 'Writing.', $00, $00; status_bar_writing shows it while copy_disk_op writes a destination sector.
Menu 4, a status line: 14 spaces and 'Formatting.', $00, $00; format_destination shows it while the drive formats.
Handler table of menus 2 and 3: two words, both clc_return ($801F), so an item run on a status line would do nothing.
Handler table of menu 0: Copy copy_command ($7F16), Restart restart_command ($80FE), Start start_command ($818A).

Menu 1's bar: '1 2 3 4 Exit', seven spaces, 'Enter side # to copy.', $00, then $1B (matched as $9B, the back-arrow key) as a hidden hot key, $00. $3A = 4 makes only '1'-'4' and 'Exit' items; the rest of the line is a hint.
Handler table of menu 1: '1'-'4' copy_side_1 to copy_side_4 ($8334, $8337, $833A, $833D), Exit and the hidden back-arrow (item 5) both utils_menu_show ($7E43).
Copy, item 0 of menu 0: sets master_drive and dest_drive to 1 (one drive, so every pass asks for the disks in turn) and falls into copy_menu_show.

Shows menu 1, the copy menu '1 2 3 4 Exit' (copy_menu_text): $3B = 1, $39 = 0, $3A = 4 (the last visible item, Exit), draw_menu_bar. Entered from copy_command, which falls into it, and called by copy_end_quiet ($7F97) after a copy.

Asks whether to format: clears format_wanted, prints message 53 'COPY SIDE n. WARNING!!! Formatting will destroy the entire contents of the destination disk. Do you want to format the destination disk (Y/N)?' with n = copy_side_number ($38), then takes keys (wait_key $022F): Y sets format_wanted = 1 and returns carry clear with A = 1; N returns carry clear with A = $CE; back-arrow returns carry set; every other key, RETURN included, is ignored.
1 when the destination is to be formatted before the first write pass: cleared and set by ask_format, read and cleared by format_destination, so a copy formats once at most. $00 in the file.

Formats the destination before the first write pass, when format_wanted is set (otherwise carry clear at once): shows menu 4, 'Formatting.', with nothing highlighted ($39 = 1 past $3A = 0), then fast-loader command 3 (JSR $FC00, A = 3, Y = track 1, X = 0). The drive code sent at boot (side 1 T18/S12-S15, drive $0300-$06FF, command 3 at drive $0363) formats by itself: header blocks with disk ID bytes $49 $50 ('IP') on tracks 1-35, then zero-filled data blocks in every sector of tracks 35 down to 1, and always answers status 0. Clears format_wanted; on a non-zero status prints message 8 'Format was unsuccessful.', waits (wait_return_prompt) and returns carry set.
Drive number of the master, 1 (copy_command): printed by print_insert_disk as 'in drive n.' and compared with dest_drive by prompt_disk_if_one_drive.

Drive number of the destination, 1 (copy_command). Nothing sets it otherwise: message 55, 'Would you like to use 1 drive or 2 for making copies?', is printed by nothing, so the copy always runs with one drive and disk swaps.

Which disk the next prompt asks for: 0 the master, 1 the destination. print_insert_disk prints message 3 + it and indexes master_drive with it; set by copy_side ($835F) and copy_pass_switch ($8386, $83AB).
The side being copied, 1-4 (copy_side): the n of 'COPY SIDE n.' and the prompts (through $38), and the side byte read_master_identity wants at $5AFF.

Ends a copy: A goes to the count $38 and message 7 '\nCopy was {0A}{0A}un{0A}successful.' prints 'Copy was successful.' for A = 1 (copy_succeeded) and 'Copy was unsuccessful.' for A = 2 (copy_failed: the {0A} switch shows 'un' only for a count other than 1); waits (wait_return_prompt), then goes on at copy_end_quiet.

Second entry of copy_end, without the message: shows the copy menu again (copy_menu_show) and clears the window (clear_window). Reached by JMP from copy_pass_switch ($8393) when format_destination fails, which has printed its own message.

One sector of a copy pass, with its own retry: A = loader operation, 0 read or 2 write, kept in copy_disk_op_operation; track in $10, logical sector in $11, memory at $FE/$FF. Shows the status line (status_bar_reading for 0, status_bar_writing for 2) and calls the fast loader at $FC00 directly; carry clear when the sector moved.

Operand of the LDA # at $7FA0: the loader operation copy_disk_op was called with (0 read, 2 write), so a retry from $7FA0 repeats it. The code after it: on an error keeps the window ($0247), widens it to column 39, prints message 29 'I/O error' (message 30 'Write protected' when the status $FC is $10) and message 32 '. (RETURN)' at column 0, row 23 with direct output; RETURN or space redraws the bar and retries, back-arrow redraws it and returns carry set. The drive code sets its status to $2B for a write-protected disk (drive $061E; the engine's disk_io tests $2B at $2817) and otherwise only to 0 or $27, so with that drive code a write-protected destination gets 'I/O error' here.
Shows menu 2, the status line 'Reading.' (A = 2; the BIT at $7FF6 hides status_bar_writing's LDA #3); nothing when it is already the menu shown ($3B).

Second entry, behind the BIT at $7FF6: A = 3 for menu 3, 'Writing.'. The shared body from $7FF9: unless $3B is already A, $3B = A, selection $39 = 1 past the last visible item $3A = 0 (so no item is highlighted), and draw_menu_bar.

$60, the opcode of RTS, between status_bar_writing's JMP and prompt_disk_if_one_drive: no JSR, JMP, branch or table word in this program, the engine or the rest of the snapshot leads here. Not reached.

Asks for the next disk only when master and destination share a drive (dest_drive = master_drive, always the case here, both 1): goes on at prompt_disk. With two drives it would return carry clear at once (clc_return).

Prints the insert prompt for the disk named by disk_role (print_insert_disk) and waits (wait_return_key): carry set when the key was back-arrow, clear for RETURN or space. copy_side calls it directly for the first master prompt.

CLC, RTS: the two-drive exit of prompt_disk_if_one_drive, prompt_disk's exit for RETURN or space ($801B), and both words of status_menu_handlers (menus 2 and 3), so a key run on those status lines would do nothing.

Prints the swap prompt word-wrapped in the window: message 2 '\nInsert ', message 3 + disk_role ('Wasteland Master' for the master, 'destination' for the copy), message 5 ' disk side n ' with $38 = copy_side_number, message 6 'in drive n.' with $38 = master_drive or dest_drive (indexed by disk_role).

Wants the master of side copy_side_number in the drive: read_master_identity; on failure prints message 56 'I/O ERROR. Check to make sure you have side n in the drive.' after a read error (A = 0) or message 57 'You have the wrong disk in the drive. Insert side n.' after a wrong identity (A = 1; the BIT at $8053 hides LDA #$38), waits (wait_return_key) and tries again; back-arrow returns carry set. Carry clear once the master is in.

Reads T35/L8 to $5A00 (fast loader operation 0, one try; $FE/$FF kept in identity_saved_fe/ff) and checks its last three bytes against a master's identity: $5AFD = $D7, $5AFE = $CC, $5AFF = copy_side_number. Carry clear when they match; carry set with A = 0 after a read error, A = 1 after a mismatch. A copy ($00 $CC n) fails here, so only a master can be copied.
Operand of the LDA # at $8083: $FE as read_master_identity found it (stored at $806A), put back after the read.

Operand of the LDA # at $8087: $FF as read_master_identity found it (stored at $806F), put back after the read; the code after it is the identity test of $5AFD-$5AFF, which leaves carry and A for check_master_disk.

Loads the saved game from the disk in the drive, the same code as the start-up's $830E: the eight pages T35/L7 down to L0 into $F400-$FBFF (read_save_page $02CF, which retries until the read works, so the BCS at $80B4 is never taken), page number in save_page_counter. No side check of its own.

Operand of the LDA # at $80B6, load_saved_game's page counter 0-7 (written at $80AE and $80CF, read at $80E2). The code after it: unscrambles the pages with the key at $F4FF (scramble_save $04E7) and compares save_checksum ($04EA) with $F4FF; on a mismatch EORs every byte at offset Y < $FF of each page with 2Y once more (net: EOR with the key alone) without testing again; then zero page $02-$0F = $F478-$F485 and clear_line_buffer ($04ED). Returns carry clear.

Restart, item 1 of menu 0: message 54 'WARNING!!! Restarting will remove all items and cash and place all parties near Ranger Center. Continue (Y/N)?'; N or back-arrow leave (clear_window), other keys but Y are ignored. Y: load_party_side_1 (the save of the disk in the drive; leaves on back-arrow at its prompt, or when $0A, the characters in use, is 0). Then for records 1 up to the count in zero page $0A (restart_record) every item slot +$BD..+$F8 (30 item/count pairs), the weapon slot +$1F, AC +$1A, armour slot +$25 and cash +$15..+$17 become 0; names, attributes and skills are left alone.

Operand of the LDA # at $8140: the record restart_command is clearing, from 1 (written at $8119) up to zero page $0A, the characters in use (CMP $0A at $8145). The code after it steps it and then, for each party from 0, points $68/$69 at the party's table (party_table_ptr $029F).

Operand of the LDA # at $8165: the party restart_command is moving, 0 up to zero page $0B, the highest party index (written at $814D). For each party the table's +$0A = 0 and +8/+9 (the party's square) = 62, 62; $09 (the map) = 0, the world map. After the loop $02/$03 (the view's top-left square) = 53, 58, which with the view offset 9, 4 that enter_map sets in $59/$5A is square 62, 62 again (in play-map the party outside the Ranger Center is at 55, 62). Then message 50 'Please put destination Wasteland character disk in drive 1.', wait_return_prompt and, unless back-arrow, save_game ($02D8) to whatever disk is in the drive, with no side check.

Start, item 2 of menu 0, as on the title screen: prints use_saved_text 'Use last saved game (Y/N)?' at column 0, row 23 with direct output (window widened to column 39 meanwhile) and takes keys: back-arrow leaves; Y or RETURN: insert_side_1_prompt, then start_with_side with side 1; N: insert_side_1_prompt, then reads the saved game of each side 1 to 4 in turn (load_save_of_side, which asks for the side) and keeps the side whose count is highest (best_count_0-3); other keys are ignored.

Operand of the CMP # at $81D1: low byte of the highest count found so far by start_command's scan (from $04; cleared at $81BB). The count is the 32-bit $F4FD:$06:$05:$04 of each side's saved game, which the game raises by byte $36 of the map's record (ADC ($61),Y at game $AF61-$AF72); the side with the largest count was saved last.
Operand of the SBC # at $81D5: second byte of the highest count so far (from $05; cleared at $81BE).
Operand of the SBC # at $81D9: third byte of the highest count so far (from $06; cleared at $81C1).

Not an entry of this program: the engine's run_menu_item JSR at $1C71 still holds $81DB, the start-up's last menu handler, when this program arrives, and the tracer followed it. Here it is the LDA $F4FD of start_command's comparison: the side's top count byte minus best_count_3.

Operand of the SBC # at $81DE: top byte of the highest count so far (from $F4FD; cleared at $81C4). The code after it: when the side's count is at least the best (carry set; so a tie goes to the later side) it becomes the best and the side goes to best_side.

Operand of the LDA # at $81F7: the side start_command's scan has just read, 1 to 4 (written at $81C9), stored as best_side when its count wins; the code after it steps to the next side and, after side 4, goes on at $8206 with best_side.

Operand of the LDA # at $8206: the side whose saved game had the highest count (written at $81F9), passed in A to start_with_side. The code after it: JMP start_with_side; the RTS at $820B by which back-arrow leaves; and at $820C start_command's Y and RETURN path, insert_side_1_prompt (back-arrow leaves) and A = 1, side 1.

Starts the game with the saved game of side A: load_save_of_side, DEC $76 so that load_item_table ($03BC) reloads item table $75 to $3100, check_side_1 ($02D5), and load_program ($03AD) with $10/$11 = 31/9: T31/L9, the game program, which replaces this one and does not return.

Prints insert_side_1_text, 'Insert side 1. (RETURN)', at column 0, row 23 with direct output (print_string_direct_at $0274) and waits (wait_return $03EF): carry set for back-arrow, clear for RETURN or space.
'Insert side 1. (RETURN)', $03 (clear to the end of the line), $00: insert_side_1_prompt's string.

Redraws the menu bar ($02E7), waits until side A is in the drive (check_disk_side $02DB: $5AFD must equal $ED, which is 0 while this program runs, so it wants a disk made by Copy, not a master) and loads that side's saved game (load_saved_game).
'Use last saved game (', $01 (inverse on), 'Y', $02 (inverse off), '/N)?', $03 (clear to the end of the line), $00: start_command's question, with the Y shown in inverse.

Prints utils_return_prompt_text at column 15, row 16 through the current output, keeping the window (push_zp23/pull_zp23): '(RETURN)', then control $08 draws the word-wrapped line, $05 waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow (wait_return) and $03 clears to the end of the line. Returns A = $18, the key that ended the wait.
'(RETURN)', $08, $05, $03, $00: wait_return_prompt's string; control $08 draws the word-wrapped line, $05 waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow, $03 clears to the end of the line.

Prints '(RETURN)' and $08 (return_key_text) at column 15, row 16, waits for RETURN, space or back-arrow itself (wait_key $022F), then prints the $08 $03 that follow the first string's zero at the same place, wiping the prompt; keeps the window. Returns A = $18, the key. The BIT $C010 at $82B3 only reads a byte; nothing uses the flags it sets.
'(RETURN)', $08, $00, then $08, $03, $00: wait_return_key prints the first string, waits, and prints the second (from where the first left $31/$32) to wipe the prompt.
Polls the keyboard once (read_key $022A): carry set when the key was back-arrow, clear otherwise (no key too). Used by print_report between fields, for its 'Press ESC to abort.'

Message 1 '\nPlease put side 1 in drive 1.' and wait_return_prompt (back-arrow returns carry set), then load_saved_game from whatever disk is in the drive (no side check: a master's T35/L7-L0 load as well as a copy's). When $0A, the characters in use, is 0: message 49 'No players to print.', wait, carry set. Otherwise carry clear. Used by restart_command and by the unreached print_report.
Prints this program's message A at column X, row Y ($23/$24) with direct output (print_msg_direct). Used for copy_disk_op's error line.
Selects direct output ($02FF), A kept, then print_msg: message A drawn at the cursor glyph by glyph.
Sets the cursor to column X, row Y and falls into print_msg_wrapped. No JSR, JMP or table in this program reaches this entry.

Selects word-wrapped output ($0302), A kept, then print_msg: the usual way this program prints its messages in the window. Also undoes hook_print_char (output_wrapped resets the engine's print vector).
Prints message A of this program's packed text block (base $8789, utils_alphabet) through the current output: $43/$44 = $8789, print_message ($0311); then report_output_on = 1.
Copy menu item '1': A = 1 (the BIT at $8336 hides copy_side_2's LDA #2, and so on down the chain), then copy_side.
Copy menu item '2', behind the BIT at $8336: A = 2, then copy_side.
Copy menu item '3', behind the BIT at $8339: A = 3, then copy_side.
Copy menu item '4', behind the BIT at $833C: A = 4, then copy_side.

Copies side A (1-4) from its master to a destination disk through one drive: copy_side_number = A; ask_format (back-arrow ends at copy_failed); master_track/sector and dest_track/sector = T35/L16, the top of the disk; $FE = 0; disk_role = 0 and prompt_disk for the master; then copy_read_pass ($83BD). Passes of up to 119 sectors alternate, read from the master into memory and written to the destination, until next_logical_sector runs from T1/L0 to track 0 (copy_pass_switch). copy_failed ($8367) and copy_succeeded ($836A, behind the BIT at $8369) go to copy_end with A = 2 or 1. The STA $10/$11 at $834B store A from ask_format and are overwritten before use.

End of a pass (119 sectors, or the disk's end). After a read pass: master_track/sector keep where it stopped, the operation becomes 2 (write) and disk_role 1, prompt_disk_if_one_drive asks for the destination, format_destination runs (once; a failure goes to copy_end_quiet), and the pass starts from dest_track/sector. After a write pass: track $10 = 0 means the side is done (copy_succeeded); otherwise dest_track/sector keep the position, disk_role 0 asks for the master, and at $83BD (copy_read_pass) the operation becomes 0, check_master_disk tests the identity again and the pass starts from master_track/sector.

One pass: pass_sectors_left = 119, buffer from $3400 ($FF = $34, $FE = 0). Per sector (copy_sector, $83DA): a pending back-arrow in $EC ends the copy as failed; copy_disk_op with copy_pass_operation on track $10, logical sector $11 (an error and back-arrow fail too).

Operand of the LDA # at $83E6: the pass's loader operation, 0 read from the master, 2 write to the destination (written at $8382 and $83BF, tested at $836F). The code after it: on T35/L8 byte $FD of the buffer page becomes 0, so the copy is written with the identity $00 $CC side where the master holds $D7; next page; next_logical_sector ($FD0B), whose table ($C930) is one track off: track 17 gives only L0, tracks 24 and 30 one sector fewer than they hold, track 18 is skipped; track 0 or the 119th sector ends the pass. The buffer skips $5A00-$8FFF, $C600-$C9FF, $D000-$DFFF and $EE00-$F4FF: $3400-$59FF, $9000-$C5FF, $CA00-$CFFF, $E000-$EDFF and $F500-$FBFF, 119 pages.

Sectors left in the current pass: 119 ($77) at copy_pass, one less after each sector ($8410); 0 ends the pass. 642 sectors from T35/L16 to T1/L0 make six passes per side (five of 119 and one of 47), as the copies observed took.
Track of the master's next sector between passes: 35 at the start (copy_side), kept at $8378 after a read pass, used at $83C7.
Logical sector of the master's next sector between passes: 16 at the start, kept at $837D, used at $83CC.
Track of the destination's next sector between passes: 35 at the start, kept at $83B0 after a write pass, used at $8396.
Logical sector of the destination's next sector between passes: 16 at the start, kept at $83B5, used at $839B.

Character report for a printer, never run: no JSR, JMP or menu table word anywhere in the snapshot holds $844A, and the menu has no item for it. load_party_side_1 (back-arrow or no characters: report_exit), message 51 '\n\nGenerating report. Press ESC to abort.', report buffer from $9000 (report_write_lo/hi), hook_print_char so that every printed character goes to report_char; then for each record from 1 up to zero page $0A, the characters in use (report_record_number): select_character, back-arrow (check_abort_key) leaves, report_lines_left = 33, message 11 'Name: ' and the name, tab_to_column 25, message 12 'Rank: ' and the string at record +$32, field width $30 = 3, then the attribute labels from message 13 (report_label_msg).
Operand of the LDA # at $84B5: the label printed before the next attribute value, message 13 '\nST =' up to 22 '\nMaxCon = ' (reset to 13 at $84AB, stepped at $84C6).

Operand of the LDX # at $84BA: index into report_attr_offsets (from 0); reused from $8557 as the record offset of the item slot being printed (+$BD to +$F7) and from $859E of the skill pair (+$80 to +$BA). The code after it prints the attribute values (print_byte_padded), MaxCon (+$1B/+$1C, print_word), 'Con = ' and CON or, when CON is 0 or negative, the condition word 43 + condition_index (UNC, SER, CRT, MRT, COM, DEAD), 'Money = $' and the cash (print_long), 'Sex: ' and Male/Female, '  Nat: ' and the nationality, the weapon and armour names (print_slot_item_name), 'Items:', and starts the item fields.

Operand of the LDA # at $855A (also read at $8571, $85A1 and $85CA): the column of the next item or skill field, 1, 21, 41, 61 and back to 1 (four 20-column fields to an 80-column line). The code after it prints each item's name, at most 18 characters (engine entry $03CB: engine message item + 36), then 'Skills and Levels:' and each skill pair with a skill number 1-35: the level (three columns), '-' and the skill's name, at most 16 characters (engine message 1-35, $035F); then new lines until report_lines_left is 0.

Operand of the LDA # at $85F1: the record being reported, from 1 (written at $846F) up to zero page $0A, the characters in use; the code after it steps it, back to report_record while it is at most $0A (CMP $0A at $85F6), then send_report; the JMP at $85FF is the item and skill loops' back-arrow exit to report_exit.

Sends the report (unreached, like print_report): a 0 ends the buffer (report_store), message 52 'Printing in progress. Press ESC to abort.', zero page and pages 2-3 copied to $CA00-$CCFF (the KERNAL will overwrite the engine's variables and jump table there), wait_key, then with interrupts off, the raster interrupt off ($D01A = 0) and the KERNAL ROM in ($01 = $36): RESTOR ($FF8A), $90-$AF zeroed, UNLSN ($FFAE), LISTEN device 4 ($FFB1), SECOND ($FF93) with A = 1, which the KERNAL sends unchanged; then $11 and each buffer byte AND $7F up to the 0 go out through the KERNAL's serial send at $ED40 (byte in $95), with no UNLISTEN after them. The border and background colours step as it goes ($D020, $D021).

Never reached: the JMP at $8680 goes back to $8671 before it, and nothing branches here. It would read $EC and stop the sending for back-arrow; with interrupts off the keyboard is not scanned into $EC anyway.

The end of send_report: CLOSE ($FFC3) with A = 1, of a file never opened ($98, the KERNAL's count of open files, was zeroed with $90-$AF, so it closes nothing), $01 back from the stack, the raster interrupt acknowledged and enabled again ($D019, $D01A = 1), CLI, and zero page and pages 2-3 back from $CA00-$CCFF.

Leaves the report: output_wrapped ($0302), which also points the engine's print vector back at the word-wrapped printer, undoing hook_print_char, then clear_window. Reached from print_report ($844F, $85FF) and by send_report's end.

Record offsets of the values print_report prints after the labels 13-21: ST $0E, IQ $0F, LK $10, SP $11, AGL $12, DEX $13, CHR $14, SKP $20, AC $1A; the $00 after them ends the list once label 22 '\nMaxCon = ' is out.
Prints message A + the record byte at ($66)+Y through the current output (print_msg): Male or Female from 26 + the sex byte +$18, U.S. to Chinese from 33 + the nationality byte +$19.

Prints the name of the item in the slot whose number is at ($66)+Y (the weapon slot +$1F, the armour slot +$25): item byte at +$BB + 2 * slot, at most 20 characters (report_char_limit), through engine entry $03CB ($0BDC: engine message item + 36), then report_output_reset. Slot 0 (nothing equipped) is not tested: it would name the item numbered by the byte at +$BB.
Turns report output back on: report_output_on = 1, report_char_limit = 0 (no limit).

Points the engine's print_char at report_char: the word at $0324/$0325, the operand of the jump-table entry $0323 (JMP $1DF8), is the address of the JMP print_char switches; bytes 1-2 of that JMP become $86FD. output_direct and output_wrapped ($02FF/$0302) write their own targets there again.

The print vector while a report is generated: character A (bit 7 set) is stored in the report buffer (report_store) when report_output_on is set. $0A, the singular/plural mark of item names, turns output off instead (so an item name stops before its first {0A}); RETURN, $09 and codes $10 and up are stored, other control codes dropped. RETURN takes one off report_lines_left and resets report_column; every stored character adds one to report_column and counts report_char_limit down, turning output off when it reaches 0.
Column of the report line's next character, 1 after a RETURN (report_char sets 0, then counts the RETURN itself); tab_to_column compares with it. $01 in the file.
